summary.name: How to Include Latency in SLO-Based Alerting
summary.one_liner: A Grafana Labs blog recap of Björn Rabenstein's KubeCon talk on defining latency-based SLOs and building multi-window error-budget alerts that count slow requests as errors.
use_cases: Designing latency-aware SLOs for a service
Setting up multi-window burn-rate alerts in Prometheus
Generating Prometheus recording and alerting rules with Jsonnet
Deciding whether slow requests should count as errors
Measuring latency at the edge with histogram buckets
Turning internal SLOs into customer SLAs
summary.what_it_does: The page is a blog recap of a KubeCon talk by Björn Rabenstein of Grafana Labs. It explains how to alert on error budget burn using a long window (for example one hour) combined with a short window (for example five minutes) so alerts fire quickly and reset quickly after an outage. It proposes treating slow requests as errors, for example counting a request as failed if it is a 500 or slower than a threshold, so there is one error budget instead of two. It describes how Grafana Labs measured this at the gateway with Prometheus histograms bucketed at 1s and 2.5s, and how it generates the rules with Jsonnet.
notable: Combines a long and short window in each alert so it pages fast and stops firing soon after the outage is fixed
Counts slow responses and 5xx errors together as one error ratio
Uses Jsonnet to generate Prometheus recording and alerting rules from a table
Grafana Labs example with 99.9% of writes under 1s and 99.5% of reads under 2.5s
caveats: Describes a talk and approach rather than a downloadable tool; the Jsonnet SLO code was said to be open-sourced only later, and its availability is not confirmed on this page
Rabenstein notes that histograms with many partitions are expensive in Prometheus
The Grafana Labs SLOs are described as SLOs, not contractual SLAs
